clue.text: Neologism going around Liberal America

indicators.note: something going around another thing encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a neologism is a freshly coined term
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A commentator notes a coinage doing the rounds among American liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW WORD wraps L to give NEW WORLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas were long called the New World by Europeans who arrived there after Columbus.

clue.text: Nice to embrace a maiden whose 26 Across is 19

definitions.note: a cross-referenced description of a person: the horseman of the Apocalypse who rides a black horse

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first word holds the following pieces inside its arms

blocks.note: nice in its older sense of subtle or delicate, as in a nice distinction
taken as written
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Something pleasant hugs a young woman, then a riddling note about what she owns.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references make a theme: 26 Across is HORSE, and the four horsemen of the Apocalypse ride black, red, pale and white horses. FINE holds A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation the third horseman, usually named Famine, rides a black steed carrying scales.

clue.text: Upright post devoid of colour

blocks.note: first meaning: a stake in a fence, as in paling
second meaning: wan, washed out

explanation.walkthrough: The word is also the colour of Death's horse, which the cross-references in 16 Across rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a pointed fence stake, and pale as an adjective means lacking colour or wan.

clue.text: Betray impatience? Fine, I would understand

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the contraction of I would
to get a joke is to understand it

explanation.surface: Someone shows impatience and is told they would understand if they waited.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless small movements are an outward sign that a person is impatient or bored.

clue.text: Partial description of Möbius strip

blocks.note: first meaning: biased, favouring one party
second meaning: a twisted loop with only a single surface

explanation.walkthrough: Partial looks like it means incomplete, but here it means biased.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased account favours one party, and a Möbius strip literally has only a single surface.

clue.text: Forest denizen on doorstep's outside with adult

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
the two ends of the word doorstep
and means together with
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A woodland creature waits on someone's doorstep alongside a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The small reddish mammal of the Himalayan bamboo woodlands lives among trees, so it is a forest dweller.

clue.text: Pet rabbit periodically covered in salon product

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
something covered in a coating sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: hair gel, sold in salons
first, third and fifth letters of rabbit

explanation.surface: A pet rabbit gets smeared with hair gel at the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit looks like the pet being defined, but only its alternate letters are used; the pet is a different small rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerbils are small desert rodents commonly kept as household companion animals by children.

clue.text: Issue close to the mother country

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: final letter of the
ma is a familiar word for mother
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A matter arises that is near and dear to the motherland.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue is a noun here, something that issues forth, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something flowing out from a source, which is what an issue in that sense is.

clue.text: In which situation sir drunkenly abandons wherries?

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are taken in jumbled order
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so these letters are dropped from the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; wherries are light rowing boats

explanation.surface: A tipsy gentleman deserts his rowing boats on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R, I and S, in any order, from WHERRIES to leave WHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The interrogative adverb asks about place, so it stands for at what location or in what circumstances.

clue.text: Sent north, Callow, whose 26 Across is 25

definitions.note: a cross-referenced description: the horseman who rides a red horse

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word north makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: raw means inexperienced or green

explanation.surface: A green recruit is posted north, followed by a riddle about his mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 Across is HORSE and 25 Down is RED: the second horseman of the Apocalypse rides a red horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation the rider on the red steed is given a sword to take peace from the earth, so he is identified with armed conflict.

clue.text: Having swallowed punch, people in general like milk

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: we can mean people at large, as in we all make mistakes
to punch is to hit

explanation.surface: Folk in general enjoy milk punch, a drink once popular in old Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and milk suggest a drink, but punch is a blow here and milk describes a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk is the standard example of the pale colour, as in milky-white skin.

clue.text: Where one eats top grub as ordered

indicators.note: an order rearranges things, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A diner orders excellent food at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordered sounds like placing an order for food, the natural restaurant sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a British pub that serves restaurant-quality meals, so it is a venue for dining.

clue.text: Extract from free lecture put in again

indicators.note: an extract is a section lifted from a larger text, so the answer is a run of letters within the next words

blocks.note: spanning the end of free and the start of lecture

explanation.surface: A quotation from a free public talk is repeated in a later speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters re-elect a representative when they return that person to office for another term.

clue.text: Headless ram? Heavens!

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter of the following word is removed

blocks.note: a wether is a castrated ram

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at a beheaded sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavens! looks like an exclamation, but it is the definition: the sky. Dropping W from WETHER leaves ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetically the ether is the clear upper air or sky, the same region called the heavens.

clue.text: Laid back guards reportedly get paid daily

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left
reported speech is heard, so the piece is spelt as another word that is said the same
guards stand around what they protect, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
to get paid is to earn, which in a non-rhotic accent is said like a vessel for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: Relaxed security staff are said to collect their wages every day.
explanation.walkthrough: LAID reversed is DIAL, which guards URN: DI-URN-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means happening every day, or active in daytime, so it matches daily.

clue.text: Uninvited guest's offence – e.g. turning up, getting kicked out

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up makes a word read from bottom to top
something kicked out is thrown away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: to take umbrage is to take offence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher's crime is turning up and being thrown out of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: EG reversed is GE; drop it from UMBRAGE to leave UMBRA. Umbra is the Latin word for shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome an umbra, or shadow, was a person brought along by an invited diner without an invitation of their own.

clue.text: Daughter upset husband whose 26 Across is 3

definitions.note: a cross-referenced description: the horseman whose horse is pale

blocks.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
as in what is eating you? meaning what is upsetting you
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A daughter upsets her husband, followed by a riddle about his mount.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset looks like an anagram signal but is a verb meaning trouble. 26 Across is HORSE and 3 Down is PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation names the rider of the pale horse outright as Death, with Hades following him.

clue.text: American protein shakes: that's poison

indicators.note: shaking jumbles contents, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
the letters of protein, rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that American protein drinks are toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakes looks like a noun, protein shakes, but it is the verb that jumbles protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is the toxic alkaloid found in deadly nightshade, so it is a poison.

clue.text: Parody secret language English eschewed

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: a code is a secret system of communication
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a private jargon that avoids plain English.
explanation.walkthrough: COD is a British informal word for fake or mock, as in a cod accent.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang cod as an adjective or noun means a jokey imitation, which is a send-up.

clue.text: Conservative running hunt whose 26 Across is 10

definitions.note: a cross-referenced description: the horseman whose horse is white

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a machine that is running is on
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: A Tory runs a hunt, then a riddle about the mount ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 Across is HORSE and 10 Across is WHITE: the first horseman of the Apocalypse rides a white horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The rider on the white steed in Revelation goes out conquering and to conquer, so he is named for victory.

clue.text: British want coffee perhaps served thus

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
want in the sense of shortage

explanation.surface: A Briton wants a coffee, with a question of how it is served.
explanation.walkthrough: Want here means shortage, not desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee taken without milk or cream is described as black, the opposite of white coffee.

clue.text: RFK here regularly travels over border for dish

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
something that travels moves about, so these letters change places
in a down entry, being over something here means spread across it on both sides

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Robert Kennedy crosses a frontier in search of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: RKEE is jumbled to K...REE, which goes either side of EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian breakfast plate of rice, flaked smoked fish and eggs.

clue.text: Defence establishment managed PC language?

blocks.note: a fort is a fortified military post
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A military base was run using politically correct speech.
explanation.walkthrough: PC suggests politically correct, but here it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortran is an early high-level programming system used to write code for computers.

clue.text: Spirited duke imprisoning European: end of story

indicators.note: a prison holds its inmate inside, so one piece encloses the other
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: dukes is slang for fists, as in put up your dukes
E is the abbreviation for European
final letter of story

explanation.surface: A lively aristocrat locks up a continental, and that is the end of the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke suggests a nobleman, but it is slang for a hand. FIST holds E, then Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A feisty person is lively, determined and full of fight, which is what spirited describes.

clue.text: This writer in Somerset town delighted

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Chard is a market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England
the setter refers to themself

explanation.surface: The writer is thrilled to be in a little West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARD holds ME to give CHARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charmed is to be pleased and enchanted, so it is a synonym for being thrilled.

clue.text: Energy-saving old car found

indicators.note: saving something keeps it held within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: crate is slang for a battered old vehicle
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an old banger that runs economically.
explanation.walkthrough: Found looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning establish. CRATE holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to bring it into being, so it means to establish or make.

clue.text: Gloomy note written about world and its end?

indicators.note: written about means written around, so one piece goes either side of the other
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
an orb is a globe or world
final letter of world, which its refers to

explanation.surface: A grim message predicts the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Its refers back to world, so its end is that word's last letter. The question mark nods to the apocalyptic theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A morbid person dwells on death and dark subjects, so they are gloomy in outlook.

clue.text: Plague from substance one used in Paris

blocks.note: substance in the sense of significance, as in a matter of import
une is French for one

explanation.surface: An illness spread by a material someone used in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Plague looks like a noun for a disease, but it is a verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune someone is to harass them with persistent requests, as a plague of nuisances would.

clue.text: Socialist article from German revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: A left-winger writes a piece by a radical German.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary sits naturally beside socialist, but it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the traditional colour of the left, so it is informal shorthand for a communist or leftist.

clue.text: Smack the Pony

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for heroin
second meaning: a small breed of equine animal

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the name of the British TV sketch show Smack the Pony; smack and the answer are both slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is drug slang for heroin, which is also called smack, and a pony is a small kind of horse.

clue.text: Centre for an audience does attract one

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the piece is spelt as a word that is said the same

blocks.note: the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: A central venue for spectators lures people in.
explanation.walkthrough: Does reads as the verb, but it is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hart is a male red deer, the animal that draws female deer in the rutting season.

clue.text: Firm's great deal with rag trade worker

blocks.note: tons means a large amount
a rag is a newspaper, and ED is short for its editor

explanation.surface: A company does big business with someone in the clothing industry.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag trade is the clothing industry, but here it splits: a rag is a newspaper and the trade worker on it is the ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned muscles are taut and well exercised, so a toned body is a firm one.

clue.text: Chiefly sombre in nature possibly?

indicators.note: chiefly means at the head, so only the first letter of the next word is kept
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: first letter of sombre
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Describing someone mostly grave in temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone mainly sombre by nature is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and grave, from the astrological belief that Saturn makes people melancholy.
